scope_note: Primary results are ordered by scientific importance, while supporting studies remain visible without being merged into the main leaderboard.

reading_guide.title: Primary comparison
reading_guide.body: The primary table reports the defended fixed-task comparison, in which direct predictors, aligned posterior framework rows, posterior decision rules, and hybrid initializers remain separated because they do not share one common evaluation contract.

reading_guide.title: Boundary studies
reading_guide.body: Boundary studies test whether the promoted representatives survive localized shifts, whether later executable families overturn the frontier, and whether direct fitting is currently interpretable in the absence of simulator provenance.

reading_guide.title: Supporting execution studies
reading_guide.body: Supporting studies establish that the inherited FitzHugh-Nagumo baseline is statistically stable, while execution configuration changes runtime far more than predictive quality on the benchmarked workloads.

primary_note: Rows below are grouped by comparability class. They should not be read as one pooled rank order.

Preferred additive-noise representative, because the clean penalty is small and the shift penalty is much smaller.

boundary_rows.intervention: raw_plus_fft256_summary12 versus raw-only and summary-only inputs
boundary_rows.secondary_delta: MSE improves 14.5%, R2 improves from 0.158 to 0.259, cov90 improves from 0.600 to 0.635
boundary_rows.resources: Same V100 training budget and four-seed evaluation block.
boundary_rows.interpretation: Observation richness mattered enough to justify promoting the richer representation before later family comparisons.

boundary_rows.intervention: Train-time drift-aware corruption for the drift010 evaluation
boundary_rows.secondary_delta: MSE improves 35.7%, R2 improves from -0.183 to 0.141
boundary_rows.resources: V100 total runtime about 126.1 s, only about 0.4% above the clean-trained SNPE total.
boundary_rows.interpretation: Localized drift failure is recoverable with matched corruption, so robustness is shift-specific rather than global.

boundary_rows.intervention: Train-time masking-aware corruption for the mask20 evaluation
boundary_rows.secondary_delta: MSE improves 50.6%, R2 improves from -0.240 to 0.216
boundary_rows.resources: V100 total runtime about 137.4 s, about 9.4% above the clean-trained SNPE total.
boundary_rows.interpretation: Masking failure is also recoverable, although the promoted path is again specific to one shift family.

boundary_rows.secondary_delta: Clean performance fails the guardrail, so no promotion is justified
boundary_rows.resources: Negative result, retained as a boundary check.
boundary_rows.interpretation: One corruption-aware model did not cover every case. The robust frontier remains plural.

boundary_rows.secondary_delta: MSE improves 8.03%, cov90 improves from 0.6354 to 0.6574
boundary_rows.resources: FMPE total runtime 166.7 s. NPSE evaluation time remains 72.7% slower.
boundary_rows.interpretation: The clean posterior frontier improved, but FMPE did not become the robust shift winner.

boundary_rows.intervention: Native BayesFlow, native Swyft, posterior decision rules, active-sequential variants, and hybrid initializers
boundary_rows.primary_delta: Coverage broadens materially, but no later branch overturns the direct clean winner
boundary_rows.secondary_delta: BayesFlow median improves MAE by 5.20% over the aligned framework row, while direct Extra Trees still stays 12.8% ahead on MAE
boundary_rows.resources: Class-specific resource costs, reported inside their own result spaces
boundary_rows.interpretation: The follow-up narrows missed-family risk without justifying one pooled state-of-the-art table.

support_rows.question: Does the inherited baseline stay statistically stable across the tested node counts?
support_rows.main_result: MSE changes by 1.78%, MAE by 0.73%, and R2 by 0.043% absolute relative percentage across the seeded reruns
support_rows.runtime_effect: Elapsed time rises from about 4.35 min to 5.24 min, increase 20.5%
support_rows.interpretation: Predictive behavior is stable, while runtime is more sensitive than quality.

support_rows.question: Which execution setting best supports broad comparative sweeps on the current Hodgkin-Huxley workload?
support_rows.main_result: Throughput rises from 29.51 to 54.75 runs per hour, improvement 85.6%
support_rows.quality_effect: No promoted quality claim depends on the broader-node path
support_rows.runtime_effect: Single-node concurrency becomes the practical default for broad sweeps
support_rows.interpretation: The practical execution default is a throughput result, not a scientific accuracy result.

data_boundary.title: Shipped data
data_boundary.body: The repository ships only the small FitzHugh-Nagumo starter dataset, which is enough to exercise the baseline code path and the smoke templates.

data_boundary.title: External data
data_boundary.body: The current Hodgkin-Huxley comparison requires external arrays, because the full tar-backed data are far larger than GitHub upload limits. The repository therefore keeps the analysis surface and the execution helpers, while the large arrays remain outside the public tree.

data_boundary.title: Result boundary
data_boundary.body: Direct clean rows, aligned posterior framework rows, posterior decision rules, hybrid initializers, active-sequential surrogates, and upstream references are shown separately because the defended comparison depends on that separation.
